items.look_for: 192 tiles of 16x32, shown 16 per row in index order (entry i at column i%16, row i/16). White = terrain in front (hides the sprite), transparent = sprite shows. Shapes should read as bottom-anchored terrain silhouettes (tree trunks/canopies, wall and building edges), not noise. masks.json states the bit layout: 64 bytes per entry, one big-endian 16-bit word per row, MSB = leftmost pixel. Entries 171-191 are blank (all-zero).
items.title: Terrain occlusion masks — 192 entries 16x32, 1 bit/pixel (ADF blocks 896-919)

items.look_for: Entry 0 = the first 64 bytes of block 896 (shadow_mem + 0*64). 16x32; white pixels are where the tile hides a sprite. Compare against the top-left cell of masks_sheet.png. Shape: a single rounded blob (a small canopy/bush), 6-12 px wide, occupying rows 5-26 and widening toward the bottom; empty top and bottom rows.
items.title: Mask entry 0

items.look_for: Entry 191 = the last 64 bytes of block 919 (shadow_mem + 191*64 = 12224..12287, the end of SHADOW_SZ). 16x32; white pixels are where the tile hides a sprite. Compare against the bottom-right cell of masks_sheet.png. Shape: entirely transparent. Entries 171-191 (the last 21) are all-zero in the ADF, so the bottom-right cell of the sheet and the whole last row plus the end of row 10 are blank.
items.title: Mask entry 191 (last)

T2.3.summary: One 1-bit PNG per terrain occlusion mask (192 x 16x32) decoded from ADF blocks 896-919 (shadow_mem), a contact sheet of all entries, and masks.json describing the bit layout and how the game indexes entries (byte 0 of a tile's terra_mem record -> maskit -> entry * 64 bytes).
